rawFindings.title: Incorrect brace expectation for single-statement blocks with leading comments under 'multi-or-nest' option
rawFindings.explanation: The change modifies the logic determining whether a block body should have braces when the 'multi-or-nest' option is specified. Previously, if the body was a single statement block, expected was false (i.e., braces not required). The patch now sets 'expected' to true if the first statement in the block has leading comments. This means it will require braces whenever there's a leading comment on that statement. This can cause unexpected failures for valid code that omits braces but has comments p
rawFindings.suggestion: Adjust the brace expectation logic so that it does not require braces solely based on the presence of leading comments inside a single-statement block, or ensure the rationale for this change is well documented and consistent with the rule's style expectations.
